newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia launches Internet shopping mall.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia launches Internet shopping mall.

text.p: Malaysian Internet access provider Jaring said on Thursday it had launched a cyber mall, allowing Internet users to shop for goods ranging from toothpaste to comics through their computers.

The Mall of Malaysia (http://www.mom.com.my) also drew its first official customer, when Minister of Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Leo Moggie stopped by the Jaring mall launch at the Internet Society conference to conduct an electronic purchase -- a 12 ringgit ($4.80) Batman comic book.

Jaring's mall offers every day items such as toothpaste and shampoo to products from luxury goods makers Givenchy, Wedgewood and Lanvin. It also sells comics, trading cards and merchandise from television programmes such as Star Trek and the X-Files.
The Mall of Malaysia has an on-screen register to display the amount spent by the customer, said Internet service provider MIMOS Bhd chief executive officer Tengku Azzman Shariffadeen.
"It can also recognise individuals who spend regularly at the mall and reward them with discounts and gifts," he said in a statement.
The mall's tenants include national airline Malaysia Airlines System's Golden Boutique, which offers designer items, and drug store Georgetown Chemist.
Tengku Azzman said the mall was starting up with about six stores. "It's good to start with that number," he told Reuters earlier this week.
"The kind of customers we are targeting are the net surfers," he said. Sales via cyberspace could lower the cost of transactions, since they occurred directly without a middleman, he said.
Delivery is centrally controlled by the mall with customers in Malaysia paying less than $1.50 for delivery the next business day for packages weighing less than 2.5 kg.

The mall is Malaysia's first stab at cyberspace marketing under its Multimedia Super Corridor project. The 15 km by 50 km (nine by 30 mile) high-technology, high-speed communications zone is being developed south of Kuala Lumpur as a test bed for information technology applications.
Malaysia has drafted four cyber laws including one covering digital signatures, which are used for electronic commerce transactions.
